questions.question: Which mountain range forms India's northern border and has the world's highest peaks?
questions.funFact: The word 'Himalaya' means 'home of snow' in Sanskrit.

questions.question: The Thar Desert, India's great desert, is mainly in which state?
questions.funFact: People cross the sandy Thar Desert on camels, which are called the 'ships of the desert'.

questions.question: The very old Aravalli Range passes through Rajasthan and which nearby state?
questions.funFact: The Aravalli hills stretch all the way from Rajasthan through Haryana and into Delhi.

questions.question: Mount Everest, the world's highest mountain, is located in India.
questions.funFact: Mount Everest is not in India; it sits on the border between Nepal and China.

questions.question: The highest mountain peak in India is ___.
questions.funFact: Kanchenjunga, in the state of Sikkim, is the highest peak in India and the third highest in the world.

questions.question: Match each landform to where it is found in India.
questions.funFact: India has almost every kind of landform: tall mountains, dry deserts, flat plains and wide plateaus.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a desert?
questions.funFact: The Nilgiris are the 'Blue Mountains' in South India, not a desert at all.

questions.question: The large raised flat land covering much of peninsular India is the ___ Plateau.
questions.funFact: The Deccan Plateau has rich black soil that is perfect for growing cotton.

questions.question: The Aravalli Range is one of the oldest mountain ranges in the world.
questions.funFact: The Aravallis are so ancient that they have slowly worn down over millions of years.

questions.question: The flat, fertile lands in northern India made by rivers are called the Northern ___.
questions.funFact: The Northern Plains have such rich soil that they are sometimes called the 'food bowl' of India.

questions.question: The white salt desert called the Rann of Kutch is in which state?
questions.funFact: After the rains dry up, the Rann of Kutch turns into a sparkling white sheet of salt that stretches to the horizon.

questions.question: The Western Ghats run along the western coast of India.
questions.funFact: The Western Ghats are home to thousands of plants and animals found nowhere else on Earth.
